coverage_notes: Every supplied observation and CSV row was considered. All registered anchor pages were visually inspected, including secondary locations. This is registry-scoped identity alignment, not a full-paper census or proof of the original curator's chosen presentation. Inputs are unchanged.
shared_qualifications: Table 5 (PDF p.7) directly supplies alloy rows and 300/500/1000/5000 ppm Cl- or natural-seawater columns at 50 C. CRA uses the corresponding numeric solution labels but calls them ppm NaCl. These mass bases are not equivalent; identity is supported by the independently named alloy and table condition series, with the conflict exposed in paired evidence. No density or ppm-to-molarity conversion is assumed, including for seawater.

Source artificial solutions are adjusted to pH 7.8 (PDF p.3); natural seawater composition has pH 8.2 (Table 2, PDF p.4). The electrochemical Epit definition is a consistent current increase indicating non-passivating pits (PDF p.6), not an inferred reversal-current threshold. The detailed CRA scan protocol is not independently verified from the inspected source passages, which refer to an earlier publication.

Source contradictions are preserved: obs_030 / CRA 30 has printed Table 5 value 1516 mV, Fig.2 labeled 17-4PH annotation 94 mV, and Fig.6 about 160 mV. obs_035 / CRA 35 has Table 5 SMO254 813 mV and PREN43.5, but Fig.6 label 254 is near PREN38 and 720 mV. obs_075 / CRA65 has Table 5 Duplex2205 629 mV, Fig.2 annotation 826 mV and Fig.6 about 630 mV. These supported identities are marked discrepant across registered locations; no decimal/label repair is guessed.

C1: interpreting the Fig.5 label Log Cl(ppm) as base-10 gives 10^2.5 = 316.23, 10^3 = 1000, 10^3.5 = 3162.28 and 10^4 = 10000 ppm Cl-. Table 5 instead uses 300,500,1000,5000 (log10 values 2.4771,2.6990,3.0000,3.6990). Actual enlarged-marker x coordinates are retained. Potential/material sequences suggest possible repeated table presentations but do not resolve the concentration conflict; these links are candidates only. At x=3, the same-alloy 1000-ppm table row is an additional concentration-based alternative where different from the possible sequence counterpart.

Fig.6 obs_110 is actually labeled 44653, near PREN43.5 and 820 mV. Candidate CRA60 follows a possible transposition of Monit44635, conflicting with Table 5 PREN38 and 721 mV; candidate CRA35 follows the plotted PREN/potential of SMO254, conflicting with the printed label. Both remain unresolved; no source identity is rewritten.

Remanit4565 and Remanit4575 are absent from the supplied CRA rows, despite their presence in the paper. Candidate-only plot links do not prove duplicate runs or identify the presentation used by the original curators. Literal CRA heat treatment None remains literal; source specimens were used without further heat treatment (PDF p.3).
